title: Auto-disable quantization on quality regression signal (route-scoped)
author: Rafael Mendes
description:
Summary: This PR wires quality regression signals (from eval-harness gating + online monitoring) into an automated safety action: disabling quantization for impacted routes (and optionally impacted customers) and forcing immediate fallback to baseline kernels. This is intentionally conservative and only auto-disables; re-enabling remains a manual action via Console/API after investigation.

Context: We’ve seen workload-specific regressions (notably JSON/tool-calling formatting) when enabling int8/int4 profiles. We already have route-level quantization controls + canary gating (PR #28879), but we lacked an automated rollback path when quality starts drifting after enablement. This implements the “auto-disable on regression” hook described in ENG-18503.

Design overview: 1) Signal ingestion: add a small internal "quality_regression" event type emitted by (a) eval-harness comparison jobs (post-publish gating + scheduled nightly runs) and (b) online monitors (format-validity + customer-defined guardrail checks when configured). 2) Correlation: resolve the impacted scope to (org_id, route_id, model_id, profile_id, profile_version). When only a model/profile is known, we look up currently enabled routes under that org and narrow by active profile resolution + GPU compatibility. 3) Action: write a route-config patch setting quantization.enabled=false and store a "disabled_reason" payload with a short code (QUALITY_REGRESSION) and a stable incident token. Action is idempotent and rate-limited per (org_id, route_id, profile_id) to avoid flapping. 4) Visibility: emit audit-log entries and metrics tags so Console dashboards/alerts can show "auto-disabled" vs manual disables.

Safety/guardrails: - Only triggers when regression severity >= threshold (default: "major"), and when confidence>=0.8 for eval-harness signals. - Cooldown window (default 6h) to avoid repeated toggles on noisy signals. - Canary-aware: if route is in canary mode (0<canary_pct<100), we set canary_pct=0 and leave enabled=false to make the route state unambiguous. - Private/Dedicated: action path is the same API surface (control plane), but for Private deployments the event ingestion is no-op unless the operator enables "quality_signal_ingest".

What’s included: - New internal service: QuantSafetyController (runs in control-plane) subscribed to quality signals. - Policy engine integration: ensures quantization is treated as disabled immediately upon config write and that fallback happens even with cached profile artifacts. - Audit log + metrics: quant_auto_disable_total{org,route,profile,reason,source}, quant_auto_disable_cooldown_dropped_total, and an audit event type "route.quantization.auto_disabled".

What’s not included: - Auto re-enable logic (explicitly out of scope). - Cross-route partial disables by prompt-set category (we only disable at the route boundary).

Testing: - Unit tests for dedupe/cooldown/idempotency and precedence with customer overrides. - Integration tests with mocked policy engine + config store to verify immediate disable and fallback decision in routing. - Replay test using a captured JSON-mode regression sample from SUP-41877 (expected: disable within one controller tick).

Rollout plan: Behind feature flag "quant_auto_disable" (default off). For beta we’ll enable for internal orgs first, then selected customers with canary-only routes. SRE runbook update in a follow-up PR will include operational overrides and how to inspect the disable reason + source.

References: - ENG-18503 (canary + auto-disable) - PR #28879 (canary rollout support) - PR #28833 (execution metrics tags) - SUP-41877 (JSON-mode regressions when quantized).
commits: control-plane: add quality signal event contract + decoding
control-plane: QuantSafetyController + idempotent disable write path
policy-engine: treat auto-disabled as hard-off (ignores canary pct)
tests: integration coverage for disable + fallback + cooldown behavior
conversation: Selene Huang (review): Can we ensure we never auto-disable on low-confidence eval deltas? Also want the audit payload to include the failing prompt-set ID(s) for triage. Rafael Mendes (author): Added confidence>=0.8 gate for eval source and appended prompt_set_ids (capped to 10) to audit metadata. Also added a metric label for source=eval|online.

Jordan Lee (review): The policy engine currently treats canary_pct>0 as enabled. If we set enabled=false but leave canary_pct at e.g. 5, we may still route some traffic depending on precedence. Please make disable unambiguous. Rafael Mendes (author): Updated patch logic: on auto-disable we set enabled=false and canary_pct=0 in the same transaction; policy evaluation now hard-stops if enabled=false regardless of pct.

Mina Haddad (review): What about profile artifact caching? If runtime has a cached quant profile, can we still accidentally execute quantized path after disable? Rafael Mendes (author): The runtime decision already checks route policy each request; this PR also bumps the config-watch priority for quantization fields and adds a test that ensures fallback occurs even if profile is cached.

Logan Wright (review): Please add a counter for cooldown drops and a field to audit log showing the cooldown window. Also ensure cost attribution tags reflect the transition quickly. Rafael Mendes (author): Added quant_auto_disable_cooldown_dropped_total and included cooldown_hours in audit metadata. Cost attribution tagging is unchanged but we verified traces flip within one config-watch cycle.

Chloe Martin (review): Any RBAC concerns? The controller is effectively writing route config. Ensure it uses a service identity and audit actor is explicit. Rafael Mendes (author): Controller now uses service principal "svc-quant-safety" with a dedicated permission "routes.quantization.write"; audit actor is that principal and includes the originating signal id.
release_notes: Internal: Added automated safety rollback to disable quantization on routes when quality regression signals are detected (eval-harness or online monitoring).
Added audit log event route.quantization.auto_disabled and new metrics to support alerting and dashboarding.
